lesson.menu_title: He Said, She Told Me — Passing On the Meeting
lesson.menu_desc: One meeting he missed, the minutes, one email, and how to pass on what people said -- 38 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 18 -- He Said, She Told Me
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Janderson Roberto Teixeira | Lesson 18 -- He Said, She Told Me
lesson.grammar_point: reported speech for statements with say and tell

listenings.text: Here is a small problem that every office has. After a meeting, somebody asks you what was said, and you have to pass it on. In English, you do this with two verbs, say and tell. They mean almost the same thing, but they work differently. You say something, but you tell somebody something. So you can say, Paul said that the report was ready, or Paul told me that the report was ready. You cannot say Paul said me. The second thing to notice is the tense. When you report, the verb usually moves back in time. Paul says, I am busy, and you report, Paul said that he was busy. Paul says, I will call you, and you report, he said that he would call. Do not worry about getting it perfect. Your colleagues will understand you. But if you get say and tell right, you will sound much more natural in every meeting.

Hi Janderson, it is Tom Becker from the Miami office. I am sorry I missed you this morning. I am calling about your client, Mr. Alves. I spoke to him yesterday afternoon, and he told me three things. First, he said that he was happy with the fund, but he wanted a lower fee next year. Second, he said that his daughter was moving to Boston in the summer, and that she would need an account there. And third, he told me that he could not come to the meeting on Friday, because he was traveling. I promised him that you would call him back this week. Could you send me a short update after you speak to him? Thanks a lot. Talk soon.

extra_audio.text: Janderson tells Rachel that he missed the meeting because he was on a call with a client. Rachel says that she took the minutes and that she will forward them. Then she tells him that Paul said the new fund was ready. He asks what the clients complained about, and she tells him they said the reports were too long. Finally, Janderson says that he will send a follow-up to his clients today.

paras: Minutes, Monday team meeting, New York office. Five people were there. Janderson was on a call with a client and missed the meeting. Rachel took the minutes and forwarded them to everybody after lunch.

First item on the agenda: the new fund. Paul said that the fund was ready and that it would launch in March. He mentioned that the minimum investment was two hundred thousand dollars. Sophie pointed out that this was too high for some of their clients.

Second item: client feedback. Rachel said that three clients complained about the monthly report. They told her that it was too long and that they could not find the important numbers. Paul promised that the team would make a shorter version by April.

Email from Rachel, two o'clock: Janderson, here is a quick update. Paul told us that he wanted a follow-up with every client before the launch. I said that you knew the Miami clients best, and Paul said that you could call them this week. I hope we are all on the same page now.
